title: Y as a Fixed-Point Operator
description: Compare a numeric fixed point cos(x) = x with the functional fixed point Z(fact_gen) = fact_gen(Z(fact_gen)).

steps.description: Find the numeric fixed point of math.cos by repeatedly replacing x with cos(x) until abs(next_x - x) < tol, reaching about 0.7390851332.
Define the Z combinator and fact_gen, then compute factorial = Z(fact_gen) as the fixed point of fact_gen.

steps.question: In the loop on lines 25-28, why does fact_gen(factorial)(n) return the exact same value as factorial(n)?
steps.answer: Because factorial = Z(fact_gen) is a fixed point of fact_gen: applying fact_gen once to factorial unfolds one outer layer of the recursion, producing an equivalent factorial function.

steps.description: Check that factorial(n) and fact_gen(factorial)(n) agree for n in range(8) and print confirmation.
Inspect via_Y and via_gen inside the verification loop to confirm they match.
